memos.scout:
The honest case for buying HEIST now is weak, and the brief shows why.

Real demand signals are present: 211 buyers and 192 sellers in the last 15 minutes, $29k volume, 226 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation with no airdrop dump, and a top-3 curve share of only 13%. The coin is alive and not a factory coin.

But the trend and structure work against it. It is 54% off its 30-minute high and down 26% over the last 15 minutes, with net flow of -13.7 SOL, meaning sellers are outpacing buyers. The sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.85, and 36% of curve buying came through bundles, which is a sign of coordinated rather than organic interest. A launch bot was present. Recent-day base rates for buying an alive coin in this window lose about 20% per trade, and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus a 30-second execution lag make that worse. Nothing here shows demand that will hold for the next 30 to 60 minutes.

Verdict: no honest case for buying now. Skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a slow distribution by insiders already in the coin, not a sudden rug. The bundle_share of 0.36 and the launch_bot_present flag suggest coordinated early wallets, and the completer_share of 0.13 means a single entity likely pushed the curve to graduation. The 30-minute return of +47% has since reversed into a 54% drawdown from the high, with net flow of -13.7 SOL over the last 15 minutes, a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.85 at launch, and sellers (192) nearly matching buyers (211). That pattern looks like holders exiting into retail demand. With only 104 SOL of pool depth, a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% fees and impact, and a bounce would need to outrun ongoing distribution. Skip.
